summary_rationale: JPMorgan Chase & Co. operates the widest-moat, highest-return universal banking franchise in the United States, generating $182.45 billion in FY2025 GAAP net revenue, $57.05 billion in net income, and 20% ROTCE on a 14.6% Standardized CET1 ratio (and 20% reported / 21% adjusted ROTCE in Q3 2026 on 13.9% Standardized CET1). Its four-pillar engine—Consumer & Community Banking ($76.0B FY2025 revenue, 75M+ digitally active users, 5,000+ branches), Commercial & Investment Bank ($78.5B FY2025 revenue, $28.0B net income), Asset & Wealth Management ($24.1B FY2025 revenue, $7T client assets), and Corporate Treasury—converts low-cost core deposits and scale technology spend into compounding tangible book value per share ($51.44 in 2016 to $107.56 in 2025, 8.5% CAGR alongside heavy dividends and buybacks). Key watches—credit card net charge-offs normalizing toward ~3.2%–3.4%, Basel III Endgame / G-SIB capital rules, non-bank private credit contagion, and post-Dimon CEO succession—are cyclical or manageable rather than structural thesis breakers.
